prompt: How many solutions does $\sin x = 0$ have on the interval $[0, 2\pi)$?
hint: Sine is the height of the point on the unit circle. Where is that height zero?

hints.text: Sine is the height of the point on the unit circle. Where is that height zero?
On the circle, height zero happens on the horizontal axis — twice per lap.
At $x = 0$ and $x = \pi$. The value $2\pi$ is excluded because the bracket is open there.

explanation: $\sin x$ is the $y$-coordinate of the point on the unit circle at angle $x$.
That $y$-coordinate is $0$ at the right of the circle ($x = 0$) and at the left ($x = \pi$).
The next one would be $2\pi$, but $[0, 2\pi)$ leaves that endpoint out, so there are $2$ solutions.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it off the graph
steps: Sketch one full cycle of $y = \sin x$ from $0$ to $2\pi$.
Count where the curve crosses the $x$-axis: at the start, in the middle, and at the very end.
The end point belongs to the next cycle, so inside $[0, 2\pi)$ there are $2$ crossings.
